purpose: Test whether logical load-bearing authority clauses explain frozen semantic outcomes better than flat all-required-source recall. This file does not modify any preregistered verdict or promotion rule and is not a product claim graph schema.

clauses.description: Authoritative evidence must bridge J.H. Park / Park Jihoon / Jihoon Park for the identity claim.
At least two independent admitted records must support that the privacy contact raised/reiterated the DPA concern repeatedly.
Direct-authored DPA wording requires Jihoon's direct email.
At least one meeting record must attribute the DPA concern/request to J.H. Park / Park rather than treat it as direct authored text.
To attribute J.H. Park meeting statements to Jihoon Park, the explicit identity bridge is required.
Earlier Privacy Counsel role.
Later Director of Data Governance role plus DPA completion/no statement that earlier position was mistaken.
Explicit first-release no-Redis decision and operational-complexity rationale.
Later 20x burst is unrealistic and does not reverse the decision.
Initial database-capacity explanation was explicitly an unconfirmed early hypothesis.
Retry increase after timeout rollout and CPU response to pausing retries.
Final postmortem identifies timeout-rollout retry storm and database CPU as downstream symptom.
09:12 start time may be established by an original or corrected admitted record.
09:25 retry signal and rollback action.
Final retry-storm root cause.
Addendum corrects start time only and preserves root cause.
Production data and subprocessors must remain in EU.
Meeting record shows DR-copy location was not confirmed and therefore is not proof of compliance.
Direct clarification includes backups and replicas in EU-only requirement.
Cobalt explicitly requires backups/replicas to remain EU-only.
Northstar standard DR may store US backups and an EU-only non-default option exists.
No-Redis rationale is operations complexity, not technical inferiority, and measured insufficiency can reopen it.
20x synthetic burst is unrealistic and calls for profiling/realistic measurement rather than automatic reversal.
Direct evidence says the DPA requirement is specific and not a general objection to cloud services, blocking the broad anti-cloud characterization.
